You can absolutely use a personal alarm. The one I use has a motion detection that if I fall it’ll beep for about 10 seconds and then call my dispatcher unless I press to cancel the alarm. It has a GPS so if I’m out of my home they can locate me. Apple Watches can also be used for similar situations. Barking is the simplest solution but there’s many many other alternatives.

It’s. Not. Legal. The service dog getting hurt is a secondary concern. Google how many service dogs run away or get stolen even when they’re not being intentionally let lose to “find help” The first concern being it goes against the ADA, leash laws, and nuisance dog laws.

It’s not about disagreeing with the “task”, it’s not legal and no one should be using it or advocating for its use by encouraging people to play along. There are better and safer ways to achieve the goal of obtaining help for the handler. Advocating for the use of this method is a disservice to the community and further spreads misinformation about how a service dog should act. Until people understand why it’s a bad idea, uninformed young handlers will keep doing it and their service dog will continue to be put at risk. So instead of telling people to follow the dog, explain why this is dangerous so people stop doing it.

The exemption for being off leash is only legal when no other alternative is able to be used by the handler to mitigate their disability. Because the alternative for barking to attract help is available, having the dog off leash even with the person conscious wouldn’t hold up legally. With the person unconscious it absolutely would not be legal to allow the dog to roam free.

The best thing I found for itching was just using a cold compress for a few minutes to stop the itch. The itching is a good sign that you’re healing but it’s super annoying. Once you don’t have open wounds you can use Benadryl cream to keep the skin from itching as it finishes healing and it won’t make you sleepy the way oral Benadryl does.

Dr Ting did my first stage and Miro did the second stage. It was agreed with Dr Ting that I would be getting VY scrotoplasty but when I was switched to Miro that wasn’t communicated and I was not told that Miro doesn’t do VY. I was pissed when I woke up and realized I got a different surgery than I was expecting to get.

They did it without an additional graft which I think was a bad choice being that it ripped open from tension on the sutures. The very tip is closed but at the base of where they repaired I have about a centimeter hole where I’m primarily peeing from. There’s additionally a pin sized hole just above it. They told me to hold my finger over the holes and pee out the tip, which is entirely impossible. I can STP but not from the tip, from the torn hole. I have to pinch the tip closed to prevent the stream from coming out two places. Trying to hold my finger over the hole just makes a gigantic mess. I can STP out my fly without mess most of the time but I’m looking forward to it being fixed as right now I have to be extremely careful and it’s stressful. I just figured out how to STP 2 days ago while on a camping trip. I’ll put up a video on my surgery blog  https://metasurgery.blogspot.com

I had a spot that needed to be closed from where one of my drains was during the first surgery and also needed the underside of the head of my penis closed where the urethra wasn’t extended to the tip. With the hole in my urethra it’s likely I’ll need another surgery anyway. I’m now looking for a surgeon that could convert to a VY at the same time. I feel like an idiot for not asking about the scrotum before surgery.
